results.fact: Where the summit day leaves the trail
results.evidence: The only route description found (SummitPost, copied by Wikipedia and others, itself from the Olympic climber's guide) says the route starts from Marmot Lake, leaving the trail three miles above Duckabush Camp and following a creek into an amphitheater on the west side of the summit - which matches beta, the itinerary summit day and the approach text ('from Duckabush Camp, continue ~3 more miles'), but not waypoints[2]/[5] ('3 mi below Marmot Lake'). USGS ground elevation at the turnoff pin is 2,831 ft (row says 3,900) and the pin sits east of the summit, the wrong side for a west-side amphitheater, which points to the waypoint notes being the misreading; but there is still only one independent route source and the row is split (waypoints on the minority side), below the internal-plus-one threshold. A second independent trip report stating where the creek route leaves the trail would settle it.

Only the SummitPost description (and pages copying it: Wikipedia, search snippets) describes the First Divide line - ridge west into a basin with a nameless lake, then a saddle and north along the ridge to the summit block. The Mountaineers route page and the online Olympic climber's guide were blocked (403 / login). No second independent source; a second trip report or the Mountaineers route text naming the saddle would settle it.

The NPS fees page lists $30/vehicle and $15/person walk-in entrance fees but does not say where they are owed; the NPS Duckabush River Trail page and the USFS Duckabush Trailhead page mention only the Forest day-use fee ($5/day, $30 annual) and the wilderness permit, with no entrance fee. Only low-quality secondary sites say entrance fees are collected solely at staffed stations. No authoritative statement either way that a walk-in entrance fee is owed from the Duckabush; an NPS statement on entrance-fee liability for boundary walk-ins would settle it (note access.fees is also an open owner decision).

results.fact: Walk-up permits and copied Staircase text
results.evidence: Already resolved: overnight_permit.where now says reserve on Recreation.gov or collect in person at a permit office, with no sites held for same-day arrivals, and mentions Staircase only as the First Divide approach. NPS wilderness page agrees: permits via Recreation.gov, phone or in person at a WIC; no sites held as same-day walk-ups; no trailhead self-registration.

Marmot Lake is now confirmed at ~4,400 ft (USGS), so day 2 (Ten-Mile Camp ~1,400 ft to 4,400 ft) needs at least ~3,000 ft, not 2,600. But the day gains sum to gain_ft (6,200) and no source gives this route's car-to-car gain or per-day figures; the rules forbid changing a day figure in isolation or computing a new total. A published car-to-car gain for the Duckabush/Marmot Lake route would settle it.
Duplicate of the earlier entry: still only the SummitPost description (and copies); Mountaineers and the online climber's guide could not be read. No second independent source.

results.fact: Summit-day gain vs camp and summit elevations
results.evidence: itinerary days[2].gainFt is 1,500 but camp (4,400 ft, USGS-confirmed) to summit (6,225 ft) is at least 1,825 ft net. Changing it would break the itinerary total that equals gain_ft; no source states this route's summit-day or total gain.

waypoints[2] ('Duckabush Camp creek turnoff') claims 3,900 ft, above the next pin 'Steep push below Marmot Lake' (3,700 ft), yet USGS reads 2,831 ft at its coordinates. Whether the pin's position or the point it names is wrong depends on the unresolved turnoff-location question above, so no elevation patch is safe.
